segments.t: Back at the agency, agent Gabriel and actress Sofia wait anxiously beside the phone for singer Julien Dore to call back. While Gabriel fidgets with impatience, Sofia tries to stay composed and avoid sounding overly eager. Listen to the scene in French first.
C'est bizarre qu'il n'ait pas rappelé.
Tu parles de Julien?
Il a dit qu'il rappellerait très vite.
Ça commence à traîner.
Tu as fait les tests ce matin!
Oui, c'est vrai, t'as raison.
Et si tu l'appelais directement?
Après tout, tu es son agent.
Juste pour le sonder un peu.
Il est en train de voir d'autres filles.
Vraiment? Il l'a dit?
Je sais pas, peut-être bien.
Il a plein de choses à faire.
Laissons Juju tranquille pour l'instant.
Bien sûr. Évidemment.
Let's walk through the conversation step by step.
C'est bizarre qu'il n'ait pas rappelé.
'It is strange that he has not called back.' Gabriel expresses nervous concern about radio silence. The impersonal construction takes a subjunctive subordinate clause.
Tu parles de Julien?
'Are you talking about Julien?' Sofia clarifies which client is on his mind. The prepositional verb specifies the topic of inquiry.
Il a dit qu'il rappellerait très vite.
'He said he would call back very quickly.' Gabriel quotes the earlier promise of rapid contact. The conditional verb expresses future in the past.
Ça commence à traîner.
'Things are starting to drag out.' The agent grows visibly impatient with the wait. The inchoative verb introduces an infinitive of prolongation.
Tu as fait les tests ce matin!
'You did the screen tests this morning!' Sofia reminds him that barely any time has passed. The temporal noun phrase points to the current morning.
Oui, c'est vrai, t'as raison.
'Yes, that is true, you are right.' Gabriel concedes that he might be overreacting. The colloquial contraction replaces the second-person subject pronoun and verb.
Et si tu l'appelais directement?
'What if you called him directly?' Sofia suggests taking initiative with a phone call. The hypothetical structure introduces an imperfect indicative suggestion.
Après tout, tu es son agent.
'After all, you are his agent.' She points out his professional right to check in. The fixed transitional idiom emphasizes legitimate standing.
Juste pour le sonder un peu.
'Just to sound him out a little.' Sofia wants discreet information without seeming needy. The adverbial quantifier softens the inquiry intent.
Il est en train de voir d'autres filles.
'He is currently seeing other girls.' Gabriel stokes her insecurity about audition competitors. The continuous progressive construction emphasizes ongoing action.
Vraiment? Il l'a dit?
'Really? Did he say that?' Sofia's cool exterior cracks with instant curiosity. The direct object pronoun stands for the statement made.
Je sais pas, peut-être bien.
'I do not know, quite possibly.' Gabriel backpedals on his unverified speculation. The colloquial negation omits the initial particle in rapid speech.
Il a plein de choses à faire.
'He has plenty of things to do.' The agent rationalizes the singer's busy schedule. The quantifier phrase introduces plural obligations.
Laissons Juju tranquille pour l'instant.
'Let us leave Juju alone for now.' Sofia decides against appearing too eager or demanding. The first-person plural imperative encourages mutual patience.
Bien sûr. Évidemment.

'Of course. Obviously.' Gabriel agrees to respect the artist's personal space. The pair of affirmative adverbs seals their tactical restraint. Now listen to the whole scene again at normal speed, and see how much more you catch.

Tu parles de Julien?
Il a dit qu'il rappellerait très vite.
Ça commence à traîner.
Tu as fait les tests ce matin!
Oui, c'est vrai, t'as raison.
Et si tu l'appelais directement?
Après tout, tu es son agent.
Juste pour le sonder un peu.
Il est en train de voir d'autres filles.
Vraiment? Il l'a dit?
Je sais pas, peut-être bien.
Il a plein de choses à faire.
Laissons Juju tranquille pour l'instant.
Bien sûr. Évidemment.
Gabriel and Sofia resolve to stay calm and wait for Julien's decision, though neither can resist watching the silent telephone. Listen to the French scene once more.
Le téléphone va sonner bientôt.
